name: @olai/bundle
//name: The application composition boundary. olai.yml selects plugin rows; generated descriptors and assets follow that list. General host packages know the bundle interface, while feature integrations depend on explicit contracts owned by their providers.
//exports:
The root exposes inert row metadata and browser module loaders; ./bundle mounts selected rows. ./assets and ./all.css describe build assets. ./testids merges identifiers exported by their rendering owners. ./tools gathers each row's own agent verbs. ./inputs adapts product boot inputs and ticket lookup into the generic host without importing capability implementations there. The import fence checks these closures independently.

THERE IS NO ./surface, ./client OR ./faces, and the three left together in #546. ./surface composed every row's members into one flat aggregate under BARE names, ./client was a typed client over that aggregate, and ./faces was three hand-written allowlists naming those bare members from a package no row could edit. A member has one tag now and it carries its owner, so the aggregate described a wire nothing serves: shrunk to what it still had a right to compose it was `@olai/surface/host`'s hostSurface verbatim, on a second identity, which is the thing that package's own doors exist to prevent. Core's grant is hostFaces beside it; each row's grant is that row's own `faces`; the flat contract the MCP adapter still needs — because serveSurfaceAsMcp builds every surface:// URI out of ONE spec's member keys, juspay/kolu#2233 — is olai-plugin-mcp/face, where the dispatch under it is scoped through the rows themselves.
//: olai.yml owns row selection; generate.ts derives browser rows, style routing and the test ID catalogue. Nothing here composes an application contract any more: a member's descriptor and its face grant are both the owning row's, and this package only selects which rows are built. Plugins never depend on the bundle; their contracts remain safe to import without activating their implementations.
//dependencies: This build declares every selected plugin so generated dynamic imports resolve. Static provider contracts are used only in application composition doors; browser and server entry graphs never acquire feature implementations merely by importing a catalogue. The Cordis runtime arrives through @olai/effect-cordis and the pinned dependency hydration, not direct framework imports. effect describes contributed schemas.
